account:
It is day 1, about 09:19. I read today's appointment book and addendum at the office this morning, returned the books, and remained there for morning business before coming to the mill for my ten o'clock grain inspection. The secretary said no letters, grain reports, or other business had arrived to her knowledge. My later appointments include council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, and an additional meeting with the neighbour at town hall at eighteen. The neighbour proposed that meeting during yesterday's tea and called it an ordinary meeting; I accepted. No special preparations were confirmed, so I asked the secretary to check with the neighbour. I have not yet heard the result.

The only unusual news I have heard this morning is Townsfolk 01 saying, near the mill and bakery, 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk are gathered nearby. The words are unclear to me: I do not know what change is meant, whether it actually happened, or who is responsible. It might concern access or transport around the bakery, but that is only a possibility, not something I have established. I have seen no change myself and have no evidence connecting this remark to the neighbour's meeting. Yesterday there was also talk of the baker carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery, which alone does not establish anything unusual. For now I should clarify the remark while keeping my mill appointment.
